subtopic_title: Addition and subtraction of numbers and place values

record_links.rationale: This worked example identifies the place values of non-zero digits in a decimal number.

heading_path.h3: Worked example 1.2: Finding place value in decimal numbers

record.evidence_quote: Write down the place values of all the non-zero digits in the following number: 73,025.048
record.prompt_text: Write down the place values of all the non-zero digits in the following number: 73,025.048
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Write the number in a place value table. Show the decimal point clearly in your table.

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
 \hline
 \text{tth} & \text{th} & \text{h} & \text{t} & \text{u} & \text{.} & \text{t} & \text{h} & \text{th} & \text{tth} \\
 (10,000) & (1,000) & (100) & (10) & (1) & \text{.} & (0.1) & (0.01) & (0.001) & (0.0001) \\
 \hline
 7 & 3 & 0 & 2 & 5 & . & 0 & 4 & 8 \\
 \hline
 \end{array}
$$

Step 2: Multiply each non-zero digit by the value of the column it is in.

$7\times10,000=70,000$\
$3\times1,000=3,000$\
$2\times10=20$\
$5\times1=5$\
$4\times 0.01=0.04$\
$8\times 0.001=0.008$

record.content_text:
In Chapter 1 you learnt that the place value of a digit tells us what the value of that digit is, based on its position in a number. You used place value tables to determine the place value of specific digits in a number. For example, the number two million three hundred and five thousand two hundred and fourteen, may be written in a place value table as follows:

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
  \hline
    \text{million} &\text{hundred thousand} & \text{ten thousand} & \; \text{thousand} \; & \; \text{hundred} \; & \;\; \text{ten} \;\; & \;\; \text{unit}\;\;  \\
    (1,000,000) & (100,000) & (10,000) & (1,000) & (100) & (10) & (1) \\
    \hline
     2 & 3 & 0 & 5 & 2 & 1 & 4     \\
    \hline
    \end{array}
$$

The place values of the non-zero digits in 2,305,214 are therefore:
$2\times1,000,000=2,000,000$
$3\times100,000=300,000$
$5\times1,000=5,000$
$2\times 100=200$
$1\times10=10$
$4\times1=4$

heading_path.h1: Chapter 5: Addition and subtraction of integers

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 5.1: Determine place values 1. Determine the place value of the digit 8 in each of the following numbers. 1. 987 2. 2,804 3. 168,417 4. 3,806,640 5. 26,008
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 5.1: Determine place values

1. Determine the place value of the digit 8 in each of the following numbers.

1. 987
2. 2,804
3. 168,417
4. 3,806,640
5. 26,008
record.answer_text:
1. 987
The place value is: $8\times10=80$

2. 2,804
The place value is: $8\times100=800$

3. 168,417
The place value is: $8\times1,000=8,000$

4. 3,806,640
The place value is: $8\times100,000=800,000$

5. 26,008
The place value is: $8\times1=8$

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 5.1: Determine place values 2. Determine the two place values of the digit 3 in each of the following numbers. 1. 363 2. 3,031 3. 32,358 4. 331,047 5. 3,158,325
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 5.1: Determine place values

2. Determine the two place values of the digit 3 in each of the following numbers.

1. 363
2. 3,031
3. 32,358
4. 331,047
5. 3,158,325
record.answer_text:
1. 363
The place values are 300 and 3.

2. 3,031
The place values are 3,000 and 30.

3. 32,358
The place values are 30,000 and 300.

4. 331,047
The place values are 300,000 and 30,000.

5. 3,158,325
The place values are 3,000,000 and 300.
